assertionsTested.reason: With an all-blocked mocked dataset, the hero summary recomputed to 0% complete with 4 blocked items and showed blocked callouts instead of a success presentation.
In a department-scoped subset, goal cards with no visible items rendered a no-updates treatment and exposed aria-disabled/data-scopable=false rather than remaining interactive.
A live narrowed state using department, status, and search survived refresh with the same controls still applied and the same constrained row set visible after reload completion.

Rows with invalid or missing Added/updated values did not make the page-level freshness badge look fresh beyond the valid 7-day boundary; invalid values stayed visibly invalid/blank and did not override the valid-date-derived badge.
After applying live narrowing and reloading, the page returned to the default overview with empty search/filters, no scope indicator, and the full 101-row result set.

Browser history was not a no-op: Back from the dashboard returned to about:blank before Forward restored the dashboard, so browser navigation did alter page state instead of remaining inert within the single-page app.
An empty CSV response produced a dedicated no-data state with no summary/controls shell shown, rather than pretending that successful dashboard content was loaded.

When a scoped live state was narrowed to zero visible rows by search text, the scope indicator remained visible and the empty-state copy repeated the active scope so the user could explain and dismiss it.
In the scoped zero-results state, summary metrics dropped to 0 done / 0 in progress / 0 blocked / 0 total and the blocked section disappeared for that subset.

Refresh only changed freshness messaging when the mocked dataset changed recency; on the unchanged live sheet, refresh preserved the existing freshness label semantics rather than resetting them just because a fetch occurred.
The 7-day threshold was applied consistently: the page-level freshness badge treated 2026-04-01 as current (7d old), while a goal with latest valid date 2026-03-31 showed stale treatment (> 7d).
Goal stale indicators were derived per goal subset in the mocked threshold dataset: goal 2 showed stale from its own 2026-03-31 row while goal 1 stayed non-stale from its 2026-04-01 row.

During a mocked refresh failure, the page collapsed from the normal top-to-bottom header/summary/goals/controls/detail reading order to only the refresh button plus retry surface, so the reading order was not preserved across load transitions.
A hard reload cleared immediately prior search/filter/scope state and returned to the default overview without any URL-encoded restoration.
Repeated refreshes showed only the canonical blocked section; no second blocked-summary surface appeared in the live or mocked blocked states.
A user-created no-match state presented recoverable empty-state copy ('No updates match your current scope, search, or filters') instead of error language or a failed-load surface.
The no-data state did not expose scope/filter explanation or any implied narrowing; summary, controls, and scope indicator were hidden while the explicit source-empty message was shown.

I could validate stale goal treatment and scoped dimming separately, but I could not produce a browser state where a non-selected dimmed card also remained stale instead of becoming an empty-state card, so this exact coexistence case was not directly testable in the current implementation.
In the Apps-scoped mocked subset, the goal-card blocked-owner signal narrowed correctly to only the visible blocked owner ('Alice') and did not retain blocked owners from broader state.
After applying live department and status filters plus search, refresh preserved the same two active non-search filters and the badge still read 2 with the narrowed row set intact.

Across normal load, no-match, no-data, refresh, and retry states, the dashboard never introduced route-like navigation controls beyond the single page; the only buttons were refresh, filters/reset, scope clear, and retry.

frictions.description: The agent-browser shell command parser repeatedly broke when heredoc evals were chained with additional browser commands using &&.
frictions.resolution: Ran browser eval/setup and follow-up click/assertion steps as separate commands against the same session.

frictions.description: Request-level network routing did not override the Google Sheets fetch in this session.
frictions.resolution: Used browser-runtime mocking by temporarily replacing window.fetch and driving the existing Refresh control for the custom CSV cases.

blockers.description: The exact coexistence state for stale treatment on a non-selected dimmed goal card could not be produced because non-selected cards in scoped views became empty-state cards rather than retaining stale treatment.
blockers.quickFixAttempted: Tested both the live stale dataset and a custom recency mock while scoping goals/departments, but dimmed cards still resolved to empty-state cards instead of stale cards.

summary: Tested 21 load-edgecase assertions: 18 passed, 2 failed, and 1 was blocked. Confirmed failures are browser history changing page state (VAL-LOAD-014) and load-transition reading order collapsing during in-place error UI (VAL-LOAD-042).
